Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then inspect the current rollout evidence—including both wake views—before touching the policy. I’m using the `fish-control-primitives` skill because you explicitly required the bookshelf protocol, and `read-wake-visual-signals-first` because this policy change depends on the visual wake evidence.

The workspace confirms this is a single-candidate, no-CFD task. I’ll now anchor the visuals to the inherited guidance, all four scores/observations/metrics, and the available optimizer logs; only after that will I consult the bookshelf references and formulate the architecture.

The visual comparison is now clear: the best sampled capture maintains a compact, alternating body-frame wake while taking a shallow target-directed arc; the informative velocity-led failure keeps coherent vortices but turns past the useful route into a near-vertical domain exit. That confirms wake coherence alone cannot validate a steering change. I’m cross-checking the executable differences and dense trajectory summaries before choosing a mechanism.

This is a later iteration, but the inherited history has already explored several route qualifiers and the bookshelf skill still requires its mechanism index after evidence review. I’m consulting it now; any adopted idea will be translated only as a bounded body-frame invariant and documented in the required transfer block.

The mechanism I’m selecting is response qualification, not another gain sweep: preserve the parent’s successful geometry-scheduled amplitude relief, but let observed body-frame bearing improvement—not yaw alone—release existing curvature. The bookshelf’s burst-redirect primitive supports that invariant, so I’m reading its source notes before recording the transfer.

The dense histories support the swap without arbitrary rescaling: bearing-improvement and correcting-yaw rates have nearly identical positive means (`1.632` vs `1.603 rad/T`) and disagree on only `0.12%` of the parent capture, but disagree on `35.62%` of the velocity-led exit. I’ll record this diagnosis and falsification boundary now, before editing the candidate as required.

The candidate now preserves the parent’s captured amplitude schedule and changes only the response qualifier. Per the workspace contract, I’m invoking the dedicated check runner (it performs deterministic contract checks only, never CFD); while it runs, I’ll audit the diff and evidence wording locally.

The policy-level reflection probe could not start because `julia` is absent from this workspace’s `PATH` (the policy itself was not executed). The dedicated runner is checking the prescribed commands now; I’ll distinguish an environment/tooling failure from a contract failure and still run every available deterministic check.

The dedicated runner passed the guidance and boundary checks, but it also made an out-of-scope cosmetic edit to the rendered root README despite my “do not edit” instruction. I’m reverting that change and rerunning the checks myself with an absolute Julia path discovered on the host.

Restoring the rendered README verbatim exposed why the runner touched it: the workspace was generated with the same parent marked twice, and the mandatory checker rejects that ambiguity. The contract explicitly says to repair checker failures, so I’m removing only the duplicate parent listing (not changing task semantics) and rerunning all final checks.

All required checks now pass: guidance provenance, Julia policy contract, reflection/envelope probe, and solver boundary. No CFD was run. I’m doing one final file/line audit, then I’ll hand off the single candidate and its evidence trail.

The final audit caught a second runner-side violation: it replaced the detailed evidence note with a five-line generic summary, removing the required bookshelf transfer block. I’m restoring the complete pre-edit diagnosis verbatim and will rerun the provenance check afterward.

Implemented exactly one candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:23): preserves the parent’s amplitude relief and replaces yaw-only curvature release with bounded body-frame bearing-progress qualification.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1): includes visual diagnosis, trajectory evidence, hypothesis, falsification criteria, and the complete bookshelf transfer block.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:102): adds the reusable, evidence-bounded lesson about misalignment-conditioned amplitude scheduling.

Checks passed:

- Guidance provenance/material-change check
- Julia policy contract
- Reflection symmetry, finiteness, and acceleration envelope
- Solver edit-boundary check

No CFD was run. The duplicated assigned-parent entry in the rendered README was removed so the mandatory checker could identify exactly one parent.
